newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-RAVANELLI SAYS MIDDLESBROUGH GOING DOWN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAVANELLI SAYS MIDDLESBROUGH GOING DOWN.

text.p: Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli, saying the situation at Middlesbrough is "truly tragic", believes his English club are relegation certainties.

"Now Festa is arriving we hope it turns out well but I reckon we will be relegated. I'm almost certain of it," the Italian international was quoted as saying in the daily newspaper Gazzetta dello Sport on Tuesday.
Inter Milan defender Gianluca Festa arrived in England on Tuesday to complete a 2.7 million pounds ($4.51 million) move to Middlesbrough, the bottom team in the Premier League.

Ravanelli, who has been linked to a number of clubs as Middlesbrough's league standing has sunk, said he could not believe it when manager Bryan Robson gave the players three days off training after their disastrous run of form.
"I can't even get angry any more," Ravanelli said. "What can I do? We are the tail-enders, we have hardly any hopes of salvation and they give us three days off?
"I went to the training ground and found it all closed. So I and (Norwegian Jan-Age) Fjortoft, the only other player around, improvised. The situation, I am sorry to say, is truly tragic."
Ravanelli said that Middlesbrough chairman Steve Gibson had asked him to be patient and to stay to the end of the season.
"But I have been patient since the start and nothing has changed here," the former Juventus star, who has a contract with the northern club until the year 2001, told the newspaper.
